text:
alice: external monitoring alerted on EU infra — spike in 5xx, looks tied to a redis failover cascade. holding all non-critical deploys. please pin any active releases you own. :warning:
deploybot: AUTOMATED: Hold applied by ops-oncall. Affected release slots moved to reschedule queue. To view: `/deploybot queue --status=paused`
ops-oncall: investigating. failover started ~02:13 UTC, primary promoted, replicas syncing. some requests still erroring due to stale reads. ETA for steady state ~20m. no customer rollback requested yet.
sam: OK — tagging the two web-service PRs I had scheduled (rev 4d2c9 / rev 9a1b7). moved them to "reschedule" in the planner.
maria: any guidance on whether we should roll back the canary that hit 502s?
dev-lead: canary 9a1b7 saw a small uptick but most failures are internal 5xx from cache layer. I don't think app changes caused it. recommend keep canary paused but avoid full rollback unless ops confirms cause.
ops-oncall: confirmation: logs show connection spikes to redis with transient timeouts during failover window. we've added read retries and are watching. no config rollbacks yet.
alice: good — can we pick new windows now? prefer tonight off-peak. @release-manager can you propose two options and pin priority?
release-manager: proposed slots: today 22:30 UTC (staggered by service) or tomorrow 04:00 UTC for full catch-up. Suggest we do small non-db deploys tonight, DB-impacting changes tomorrow morning. Thoughts? :calendar:
sam: agree with staggered approach. I'll split my batch — non-db items into tonight's slot, db migrations to tomorrow.
maria: +1. also adding smoke tests to the reschedule checklist so we don't reintroduce the failure vector.
deploybot: NOTE: When releases are rescheduled they keep their original version pins. Use `deploybot reschedule <slot>` to move items.
ops-oncall: we'll mark the incident as monitoring-investigating and update status in #incidents. will call when replicas are caught up. ETA now ~15m.
alice: thanks. leaving hold in place until ops gives the all-clear. @deploybot leave a note on each paused slot: "paused - incident: redis failover". :white_check_mark:
release-manager: copying final plan into the release calendar. I'll notify teams and update release notes template with the incident tag so downstream owners can triage if regressions appear.
deploybot: ACTION: Paused slots annotated. Reschedule suggestions recorded.
ops-oncall: 12m — primary CPU normalized, replica lag decreasing. will update again at 0.
alice: ack, standing by.
